A 7-foot-1 center known for his shot-blocking and perimeter shooting, as well as his reverse dunks, Huff played four seasons of college basketball for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]], where he was part of the program's [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA championship]] run and earned [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] and ACC All-Defensive Team honors as a senior. Undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft|2021]], Huff developed through multiple stints in the [[NBA G League]] and was named the [[NBA G League Defensive Player of the Year]] in 2023. He played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Washington Wizards]] and [[Denver Nuggets]] before earning rotation minutes with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] during the 2024–25 season. In July 2025, Huff was acquired by the Pacers, where he established himself as a productive rim protector and stretch five off the bench. ==High school career== Huff was a four-year varsity basketball player for [[Voyager Academy]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], where he was coached by his father, Mike.{{cite web |last1=Warnock |first1=W. E. |title=Voyager Academy's father-son Huff team gets one last game together in championship |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/high-school/article65235357.html |website=[[The News & Observer]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=March 10, 2016}} On January 21, 2016, as a senior, he became his school's all-time leading scorer.{{cite web |last1=Best |first1=Bonitta |title=Huff voyages into the record books |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/community/durham-news/dn-sports/article56956153.html |website=[[The News & Observer]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=January 27, 2016}} Huff led his team to the Class 1A state title, earning [[most valuable player]] honors after recording a [[double (basketball)|triple-double]] of 14 points, 14 rebounds and 10 blocks in the final.{{cite web |last1=Warnock |first1=W. E. |title=Jay Huff's triple-double leads Voyager Academy to 1A basketball title over Winston-Salem Prep |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/high-school/article65700282.html |website=[[The News & Observer]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=March 12, 2016}} He finished the season averaging 16.3 points, 10.1 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Ratcliffe |first1=Jerry |title=UVa's Jay Huff is hungry for more |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/uva-s-jay-huff-is-hungry-for-more/article_66ac02f4-e201-5063-94fd-97aa15a0d730.html |website=[[The Daily Progress]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=November 10, 2017}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Huff committed to play college basketball for [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=Jay Huff to Virginia: Cavaliers Land 4-Star PF Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2472790-jay-huff-to-virginia-cavaliers-land-4-star-pf-prospect |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=May 21, 2015}} Growing up minutes from the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]], Huff was familiar with the region’s major basketball programs, but his thin frame and long-term development profile made him a better fit for [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]]’s system at Virginia. The Cavaliers recruited him early, offering a clear development path in their defense-oriented scheme, and Huff committed to Virginia in May 2015. ==College career== Huff redshirted his first year at Virginia to improve his strength and conditioning, gaining about {{convert|30|lb|kg|0}} before the start of the 2017–18 season. He appeared in 12 games as a redshirt freshman, averaging 3.4 points and 1.9 rebounds in 8.8 minutes per game on 68 percent shooting from the field.{{cite web |last=Darney |first=Caroline |title=Jay Huff is developing in front of our eyes, and it's magical |url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2019/1/25/18194181/ncaa-basketball-virginia-cavaliers-jay-huff-developing-playing-time-hoonicorn |website=Streaking the Lawn |publisher=SB Nation |date=January 29, 2019 |access-date=April 21, 2020}} Ahead of the 2018–19 season, Huff underwent surgery for a torn labrum that sidelined him for three to four months.{{cite web |last1=Blum |first1=Sam |title=Jay Huff out 3-4 months with torn labrum |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/sports/jay-huff-out---months-with-torn-labrum/article_562b07be-385f-11e8-898b-2702de40bf54.html |website=[[The Daily Progress]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=April 4, 2018}} He returned to contribute to Virginia’s national championship run, averaging 4.4 points in 9.3 minutes per game on 60.4 percent shooting.{{cite web |title=Jay Huff |url=https://virginiasports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jay-huff/6749 |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |accessdate=April 21, 2020}} He delivered several high-impact performances, including 17 points and six blocks in a win over Georgia Tech on January 18, 2020 {{cite web |title=Jay Huff |url=https://virginiasports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jay-huff/6749 |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |accessdate=April 21, 2020}} and a near–triple-double of 15 points, 10 blocks and nine rebounds in a victory over Duke, making him the second player in program history with at least 10 blocks in a game.{{cite web |last1=Gatto |first1=Tom |title=Virginia's Jay Huff enters Ralph Sampson territory by standing tall vs. Duke |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/jay-huff-virginia-duke-blocked-shots-ralph-sampson/7i6pqwamoo981svewdwyrqsm9 |website=[[Sporting News]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=February 29, 2020}} Huff was a member of Virginia’s 2019 championship core alongside future NBA players [[De'Andre Hunter]] and [[Ty Jerome]], with both later acknowledging his impact on that title team.{{cite web |last=Easterling |first=Chris |title=Cavaliers’ Ty Jerome and De’Andre Hunter reunited as former Virginia champions |url=https://eu.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/pro/cavs/2025/02/25/cleveland-cavaliers-ty-jerome-deandre-hunter-trade-cavs-teammates-virginia-2019-ncaa-champions/80066748007/ |website=Akron Beacon Journal |date=February 25, 2025 |access-date=February 26, 2025}} As a junior in 2019–20, Huff set career highs with 8.5 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.0 blocks per game while anchoring one of the nation’s best defenses. His development continued into his senior season, when offseason training—reportedly involving more than 18,000 practice shots with longtime family friend and coach [[Bob MacKinnon]]—helped him become one of college basketball’s most efficient two-way players.{{cite news |last=Hamilton |first=Brian |title=At Virginia, Jay Huff at long last has his shot |url=https://theathletic.com/2363074/2021/02/09/virginia-basketball-jay-huff/ |work=The Athletic |date=February 9, 2021 |access-date=February 26, 2025}} In 2020–21, Huff averaged 13.0 points, 7.1 rebounds and 2.6 blocks per game while shooting 58.5 percent from the field and 38.7 percent from three, earning Second-team All-ACC and ACC All-Defensive Team honors. Following the 2019–20 season, Huff entered the 2020 NBA Draft process before withdrawing and returning for his senior year.{{cite web |last=Conlin |first=Bennett |title=Jay Huff withdraws from NBA Draft, plans to return for senior season at Virginia |url=https://dailyprogress.com/sports/jay-huff-withdraws-from-nba-draft-plans-to-return-for-senior-season-at-virginia/article_32060571-d2b7-5882-a4ee-b825e09575db.html |website=The Daily Progress |date=August 1, 2020 |access-date=August 1, 2020}} After the 2020–21 season, he declared for the 2021 NBA Draft. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles / South Bay Lakers (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Huff joined the [[Washington Wizards]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Wizards announce 2021 Summer League roster|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-announce-2021-summer-league-roster|work=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}} On September 21, 2021, he signed with the Wizards,{{cite tweet|author=Washington Wizards|number=1440478129382846464|title=OFFICIAL: We've signed the following players to Exhibit 10 contracts: □ Jaime Echenique □ Jordan Goodwin □ Jay Huff □ Jordan Schakel|user=WashWizards|date=September 21, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}} but was waived on October 13.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Wizards Cut Jay Huff, Jordan Schakel|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/wizards-cut-jay-huff-jordan-schakel.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} On October 18, 2021, Huff signed a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Jay Huff to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-jay-huff-two-way-contract-211018|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} On January 12, 2022, he was waived.{{Cite web|title=Lakers Sign Sekou Doumbouya to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-sekou-doumbouya-two-way-contract-waive-jay-huff-1-12-22|access-date=January 12, 2022|website=NBA}} On January 16, 2022, Huff was re-acquired by the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{Cite web|title=South Bay Lakers on Twitter: "OFFICIAL: The #SBLakers have acquired Jay Huff as a returning rights player. In a related move, the team has waived Willie Jackson"|url=https://twitter.com/SouthBayLakers/status/1482843162401935361|access-date=January 18, 2022|website=Twitter}} Huff joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612747/lakers |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com}} In his Summer League debut for the Lakers, Huff scored nine points and seven rebounds in a 100–66 win against the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Miami Heat Jul 2, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-mia-1322200001/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com}} On July 27, 2022, Huff signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=Lakers Sign Jay Huff |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-jay-huff-072622?amp=1 |access-date=July 27, 2022 |date=July 27, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} He was waived on October 15, 2022.{{Cite tweet |user=Lakers |number=1581390642927673344 |title=The Lakers have requested waivers on guards Shaquille Harrison and Nate Pierre-Louis and center Jay Huff.}} He subsequently re-joined South Bay. ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2023)=== On March 2, 2023, Huff signed a two-way contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |date=March 2, 2023 |title=Wizards Sign Jay Huff to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-jay-huff-to-two-way-contract |access-date=March 2, 2023 |website=NBA}} On April 4, he was named [[NBA G League Defensive Player of the Year Award|NBA G League Defensive Player of the Year]] after leading the league with 4.0 blocks per game.{{cite web|title=Jay Huff Named 2022-23 KIA NBA G League Defensive Player of the Year|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/jay-huff-named-2022-23-kia-nba-g-league-defensive-player-of-the-year|website=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2023|access-date=April 4, 2023}} On July 3, 2023, Huff joined the [[Houston Rockets]] Summer League team.{{cite web|title=Rockets Summer League roster 2023: Details of players, coaches, schedule and more |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/rockets-summer-league-roster-2023-details-players-coaches-schedule}} ===Denver Nuggets / Grand Rapids Gold (2023–2024)=== On July 18, 2023, Huff signed a two-way contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN GILLESPIE, HUFF AND KEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-gillespie-huff-and-key-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2024–2025)=== [[File:Grizzlies visit the 164th AW! (240910-F-UM667-7699).jpg|thumb|right|Huff (left) with [[Memphis Grizzlies]] rookie [[Jaylen Wells]] at [[Memphis Air National Guard Base]] in 2024]] On July 24, 2024, Huff signed a two-way contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Jay Huff to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jay-huff-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=July 24, 2024}} On October 26, he scored a career high eighteen points in a home victory against the [[Orlando Magic]] and two days later, he signed a four-year, $10.1 million contract with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Jay Huff to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-jay-huff-to-multi-year-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} Huff made 64 appearances (two starts) for Memphis during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 6.9 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 0.6 assists. === Indiana Pacers (2025–present) === On July 6, 2025, Huff was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for a 2029 second-round pick and a 2031 second-round pick swap.{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Acquire Jay Huff|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-acquire-jay-huff|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 6, 2025}} On November 19, Huff scored 20 points, five rebounds, and four assists against the [[2025–26 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]]. On January 16, 2026, Huff scored a career-high 29 points and grabbed nine rebounds against the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]]. In the 2025-2026 season, Huff played in all 82 games and had the third highest blocks per game in the league, recording averages of 9.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 1.9 blocks.{{cite news |last1=Dopirak |first1=Dustin |title=In Pacers' injury-ravaged season, Jay Huff plays all 82 |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2026/04/13/in-pacers-injury-ravaged-season-jay-huff-plays-all-82/89585851007/ |date=13 April 2026 |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=The Indianapolis Star}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A. Huff's parents are former [[college basketball]] players. His father, Mike, played for [[Pacific Lutheran University]], and his mother, Kathy, played for [[West Virginia Mountaineers women's basketball|West Virginia]]. Mike was the director of the Michael W. Krzyzewski Human Performance Laboratory at [[Duke University]].{{cite web |last1=Needelman |first1=Josh |title=Higher calling: Jay Huff's faith has been tested — and validated — at Virginia |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/sports/cavalierinsider/higher-calling-jay-huffs-faith-has-been-tested-and-validated-at-virginia/article_27b0cf74-2a7e-11e9-b722-cfb470d4fa82.html |website=[[The Daily Progress]] |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |date=February 7, 2019}} Huff is a member of the [[Chi Alpha (Christian Fellowship)|Chi Alpha]] Christian fellowship at the [[University of Virginia]] and aspires to become a minister when he retires from basketball. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://virginiasports.com/player/jay-huff/ Virginia Cavaliers bio] {{Indiana Pacers current roster}} {{navboxes|list= {{NBA G League Defensive Players of the Year}} {{2019 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball navbox}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Huff, Jay}} [[Category:1997 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Durham, North Carolina]] [[Category:Capital City Go-Go players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Denver Nuggets players]] [[Category:Grand Rapids Gold players]] [[Category:Indiana Pacers players]] [[Category:Los Angeles Lakers players]] [[Category:Memphis Grizzlies players]] [[Category:Memphis Hustle players]] [[Category:South Bay Lakers players]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:United States men's national basketball team players]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Washington Wizards players]]
